recognize_zh: 中央大細胞核呈雙葉、染色質中度凝集，外圍一圈窄而深藍、幾乎無顆粒的細胞質，體積明顯大於周圍骨髓前驅細胞，屬未成熟巨核細胞。
features: Large cell, several times the size of surrounding myeloid precursors, with a high N:C ratio
Bilobed nucleus with moderately condensed chromatin and no distinct nucleoli
Narrow rim of deeply basophilic, agranular cytoplasm with a slightly irregular border
Absence of the abundant granular cytoplasm and multilobation of mature megakaryocytes
Background of maturing granulocytes (myelocytes, metamyelocytes, bands), an eosinophilic myelocyte, erythroid precursors and lymphocytes
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large immature megakaryocyte with a bilobed nucleus, moderately condensed chromatin and a narrow rim of deeply basophilic agranular cytoplasm. The surrounding marrow shows orderly granulocytic maturation with eosinophilic precursors and erythroid cells. No dysplastic separated nuclear lobes or blast clusters are present. Findings are consistent with an immature megakaryocyte, a feature that increases with high platelet turnover.

ddx.vs: A megakaryoblast is smaller, with a single round nucleus, fine chromatin, nucleoli and cytoplasmic blebs, rather than a bilobed nucleus with condensing chromatin.
Micromegakaryocytes are small, about promyelocyte-sized, with a single round nucleus and mature pink granular cytoplasm, unlike this large basophilic cell.
Proerythroblasts are smaller, with a single round nucleus, visible nucleoli and deep blue cytoplasm with a perinuclear clear zone, and lack nuclear lobation.
